meta.title: Reproducing Chloe: does the instruction-tuning mix matter?
meta.subtitle: Chloe's released model trains on Opus trait data PLUS a general instruction-tuning (IT) mix; our runs had been omitting it. We reconstructed the exact IT mix from public datasets and trained the full recipe. Question: does adding the IT mix change where the model lands? Capability = GPQA-Diamond strict@20k thinking-on (n=198). Trait = agentic-misalignment murder rate (n=100, gpt-4.1 grader) — all three trained arms CO-MEASURED in one batch (see notes).
meta.y_label: AM murder rate → lower is more aligned

conditions.label: base (Qwen3-32B)
conditions.note: No adapter. The capability ceiling and misalignment floor we try not to drift back toward. (murder from the stable base reference.)

conditions.label: Chloe — released checkpoint
conditions.note: Her released aft-cot model organism — Opus trait tokens + the general instruction-tuning mix.

conditions.label: Repro — trait data only
conditions.note: SFT on the Opus philosophy-spec tokens only — NO instruction-tuning mix. What our prior runs used.

conditions.label: Repro — + instruction mix
conditions.note: The full recipe: Opus trait tokens + the reconstructed 10k IT mix (rendered per-sample thinking-off so it doesn't collapse reasoning).

notes: The IT mix barely moves the point: trait-only (GPQA 0.48 / murder 0.06) vs + IT mix (0.51 / 0.08) are within noise of each other. Adding the instruction-tuning data — the 'exact repro' ingredient — does not change where the model lands. The prior no-IT runs were a valid stand-in for Chloe.
Both our repros sit deeper-trait than Chloe's released checkpoint (murder 0.06–0.08 vs 0.20) at similar capability — our reproduction installs the trait at least as strongly as the release.

AM is CO-MEASURED for the three trained arms in one eval batch. This matters: Chloe's released AM reads anywhere from murder 0.05 to 0.20 across batches (grader + n=100 + setting noise), so only a single co-measured batch gives the true relative ordering. GPQA is reproducible across batches (greedy, strict parse, no grader) so it is reused.

Getting the IT mix right required rendering the non-CoT instruction data with thinking OFF per-sample; rendering everything thinking-on injects an empty <think></think> on the IT samples and collapses the model to skip reasoning (a failed first attempt sat at GPQA 0.31 / murder 0.38, every rollout empty-think). That arm is excluded here.

Recipe (all trained arms): Qwen3-32B, LoRA r64/α128, 1 epoch, lr 1e-4 cosine, seq 8192. IT mix = 10k samples (No Robots, Tulu3-IF, NuminaMath, smoltalk subsets, LIMA, LongAlign) reconstructed from public data at Lee et al.'s exact table counts.
